company_info.name: Eastport University
company_info.description: A R1 university hosting a growing newly hired research-track faculties across multiple colleges.

persona.name: Aisha Rahman
persona.responsibilities: Coordinates orientation, document collection, and ongoing compliance communications for new faculties.

example_dr_questions: What is the workflow to onboard a newly hired tenured-track faculty?
insights: New hire is an Assistant Professor (tenure-track) in the College of Engineering with a start date of Aug 15; offer has been signed and the chair wants all access ready by first day.
Appointment is 9-month with summer salary eligible, so the department will submit Eastport’s Position Data Form (PDF-7) with FTE = 1.0 and “summer comp: eligible” checked.

Faculty is a non-U.S. citizen currently outside the U.S. and will enter in J-1 “Professor” status; the department will open an ISSS case and provide the required passport bio page + CV + offer letter for the DS-2019 request.
Background check is required because the appointment is benefits-eligible; the hire will complete the BGC-2 authorization through EastportWorks when the link is triggered.

The faculty will be paid via payroll (not stipend), so I-9 will be completed in person during check-in; direct deposit and tax withholding will be completed in the HR portal beforehand.
The department prefers to complete benefits enrollment during the first week; the hire will attend the faculty orientation and schedule a one-on-one benefits consult.

The faculty will be a PI with a $300k startup package and will need purchasing authority; the department expects an index to be created and will route the Startup Fund Authorization (SFA-3) with “>$250k” selected.
A compliance reminder cadence is needed (visa document tracking + annual COI update) because the faculty will pursue sponsored research in year one.

The faculty needs access to a wet lab space in the Engineering Research Building, so a Lab Access Request (LAR-5) will be submitted and EH&S trainings will be scheduled before keys are issued.
The faculty is scheduled to teach one graduate course in the first semester, so a teaching setup is needed (instructor-of-record entry, LMS course shell, and classroom tech orientation).
Research activities in the first 90 days are expected to be non-human-subjects and non-animal, so IRB/IACUC protocols will not be submitted during initial onboarding.
The faculty will require building access, email, VPN, and a university laptop; the department will submit the IT Access Request (IT-8) for network groups and door access.
